sonnet.problem: The story card right before it (card 10) says 'The young officers march out first.' The scouts' report on card 11 is that men are marching out of Samaria, so card 10 gives the answer away. It also rules out the wrong answers about Ahab asking for peace and more kings coming.
sonnet.rule: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

sonnet.problem: The fill-in-the-blank is a line of Ben-hadad's oath with the key word removed. The baker has not seen the wording ('dust'), so the pick comes down to guessing the next word of the line.
sonnet.rule: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

sonnet.problem: The card asks what Ahab's saying about armor means and treats 'Don't brag before the battle's over' as the fact. The passage does not say what the saying stands for.
sonnet.rule: Leave open what the text leaves open: ... This includes what a picture means. He retells the picture as the text gives it and says what it stands for only when the passage says so.

sonnet.problem: The joke does not click for a baker. It compares the kings staying in their tents at noon to 'a long break even for a stamper who spent YEARS in a junk drawer,' but the drawer years were not a break, so the comparison does not match the action. It also says the kings are 'still' in their tents, which adds a time the text does not give.
sonnet.rule: The everyday comparison must have the same action. ... If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
